name: AnyPS5
description: Tool for automatic PS5 executables porting to Linux and Windows
one_liner: Takes a PlayStation 5 game and converts it so it can run directly on a Windows or Linux PC, without a PS5 or an emulator.
buyer: There isn't really one. This is a hobbyist reverse-engineering project for enthusiasts who want to run specific PS5 games on PC; it's not aimed at anyone who'd pay for it.
business_use_cases: A retro-gaming hardware shop could offer 'play your PS5 library on this mini-PC' setup services, but the legal and compatibility risk makes this a bad business bet.
A hobbyist YouTuber documents compatibility testing for ad revenue, which is really a content play, not a product built on the tool.
A systems programmer uses the public relinker/shader-recompiler code as a learning resource for their own unrelated binary-translation project.

money_ideas.idea: None that are defensible: selling access to or services around running PS5 executables on unauthorized hardware invites takedown and legal risk from Sony.

steal_this: Don't build a business on this one. If anything, write a technical blog post about how the shader recompiler works, for programmer audience/ad revenue only.
